week_thesis: AI infrastructure super-cycle roaring: Broadcom (AVGO) reports Q2 Wednesday June 3 after close — consensus +47% YoY revenue to $22B with AI semi contributing ~$10.7B — a potential sector catalyst for the full AI hardware cohort. S&P 500 RSI at 73 (overbought broadly), so selectivity is critical: own AI hardware leaders with catalysts and dip setups, trim positions that have exhausted upside. NVDA post-earnings dip to $212 (-10% from $235.74 ATH on May 14) is the cleanest buy setup this week: RSI 49.8 neutral, 61-analyst Strong Buy consensus, average 12-month target $297-$307 (+40-45% upside), FY2026 revenue +65% YoY. AMD scores #1 in universe (RS60=+66% vs SPY, RSI 52.8, data center $5.8B +57% in Q1); Meta signed 6GW multi-year GPU deal and hyperscaler MI450 demand is exceeding internal forecasts. Capital source: close FLEX (locked in +16.4% at ATH with only ~2% remaining to $157.50 target), VIAV (analyst target $39.25 fell below $49.50 entry — thesis broken), and ASTH (lagging healthcare sector -15.1% RS60, medium conviction, stop-loss at $35.94 in jeopardy). PLTR holding strong at +15.9% gain post-9% May 29 surge on Dell earnings AI partnership validation; analyst mean target $193. AVGO and CRWD both report June 3 — blackout. Friday NFP report is primary macro risk for the week.

buys.reasoning: Post-earnings dip to $212.49 (-10% from May 14 ATH of $235.74) creates a clean mean-reversion entry. RSI 49.8 (neutral — no excess). FY2026 revenue $215.94B (+65% YoY), EPS beat, $80B buyback authorized. CEO Jensen Huang called demand 'parabolic' on Agentic AI. 61 analysts Strong Buy consensus; average 12-month target $297-$307 = +40-45% upside from current price; Tigress Financial targets $425 (+100%). Stock has declined 8 of last 10 days, flushing short-term momentum chasers. Broadcom earnings June 3 (if strong) would re-accelerate the AI semi trade and directly benefit NVDA. No earnings risk this week.

Universe's #1 ranked candidate (score +0.2338, RS60=+66% vs SPY, RSI 52.8, dip5d +5%). Q1 2026 data center revenue $5.8B (+57% YoY), record server CPU revenue +50%+ across cloud and enterprise. CEO Lisa Su raised server CPU TAM forecast from ~$60B to >$120B growing >35% annually by 2030. Meta signed multi-year deal for 6GW of AMD GPUs for AI data centers. Minor 5-day pop (+5%) but well within tolerance given 66% RS60 lead over SPY.

close_reasoning.FLEX: FLEX hit all-time high of $154.25 on May 29 from $132.46 entry (+16.4% gain, ~$2,425 on 112 shares). Analyst consensus 12-month target is $157.50 — only 2.1% remaining upside. Risk/reward has compressed significantly: locking in +16% now and redeploying into NVDA (40%+ upside) or AMD (66% RS60) is superior capital allocation. Spin-off announcement of Cloud & Power Infrastructure segment was a catalyst already reflected in the price. Strong buy consensus, but the easy money has been made. Close and recycle capital.
close_reasoning.VIAV: Analyst target $39.25 now falls meaningfully below entry of $49.50 — thesis broken. VIAV was entered May 25 on the premise of 'discount to analyst target with strong sector momentum' but the current consensus target is ~21% below our basis. With last known P&L at +2.19% ($334 gain on May 27), close while modestly profitable before further deterioration. Limited AI connectivity catalyst. The US Communications sector has outperformed broadly, making further re-rating less likely.
close_reasoning.ASTH: Astrana Health (ASTH) sits in the healthcare sector which has lagged the broader market by -15.1% over 60 days. Medium conviction position entered May 25 at $37.83 with stop at $35.94 (-5% threshold). Healthcare continues to lag as AI/tech dominates capital flows. No near-term catalyst visible. Last known P&L: -1.21% (-$185). Proactive close avoids stop-loss trigger and stop uncertainty from API access limitations; frees capital for higher-conviction AI hardware names.
